reproduction_target: Construction of a haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) epigenetic ageing clock from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of pectoral fin tissue (n=140): WGBS read QC/trimming, Bismark alignment to the haddock reference genome, deduplication, methylation extraction and CpG strand merging, coverage/presence filtering with bedtools, bisulfite conversion-efficiency estimation against E. coli ASM584v2, low-variance and SNP-overlapping CpG filtering (caret, BS-Snper), Bayesian GLMM age-association screening (rstanarm stan_glmer), missing-data imputation (mice), lasso/elastic-net model selection with a 70/30 train-test split (glmnet), genomic-context annotation (GenomicRanges/IRanges) and STRING functional enrichment. Fin/otolith collection, otolith annuli ageing, DNA extraction and Pico Methyl-Seq library prep + NovaSeq sequencing are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v1 full-text Methods prose. The JATS source XML and the landing page returned HTTP 403; the full text was retrieved by curl of the v1.full HTML (HTTP 200 after a 429 back-off). The Data Availability statement cites https://github.com/emmastrand/Epigenetic_ageing as holding 'all data and code used to produce results, and complete analyses', but that repository returns HTTP 404 and is absent from the public repository list of the GitHub user emmastrand, so NO README prose could be read and no env-capture claim from the repo could be inspected. capture_claim is therefore derived from the paper prose alone, which pins exact versions for essentially every named tool but claims no lockfile, container, or conda environment. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Raw WGBS read quality assessment with FastQC (v0.11.9) on the Northeastern University Discovery HPC cluster (default invocation)
Aggregation of per-sample QC into a MultiQC (v1.16) report used to choose trimming parameters
Paired-end adapter/quality trimming with TrimGalore! (v0.6.5) using --clip_r1 10, --clip_r2 10, --three_prime_clip_r1 10, --three_prime_clip_r2 10

Bisulfite alignment of trimmed reads to the haddock reference genome (cited only as reference 85, no assembly accession/version inline) with Bismark (v0.24.2) align + Samtools (v1.9), parameters --relax_mismatches, --num_mismatches 0.6, --non-directional
Duplicate removal from aligned BAMs with Bismark deduplicate_bismark (v0.24.2, defaults; deduplicated BAMs deposited on OSF)
Methylation call extraction with Bismark bismark_methylation_extractor (v0.24.2) — no parameters stated; global methylation percentage also taken from this step
Top/bottom strand merge with Bismark coverage2cytosine (v0.24.2), parameters --merge_CpG and --zero_based

Filtering to CpG sites present in >=90% (and separately 100%) of samples at 10X coverage using intersectBed and multiIntersectBed from bedtools (v2.29.0) — exact command lines / thresholds implementation not given in prose

Bisulfite conversion-efficiency estimation: trimmed reads aligned with the same Bismark (v0.24.2)/Samtools (v1.9) steps to E. coli str. K-12 MG1655 (ASM584v2, RefSeq GCF_000005845.2), efficiency = (U_CHH + U_CHG)/((U+M)_CHH + (U+M)_CHG); samples <96% excluded from model generation
Low-variance CpG filtering in R (v4.2.0) with caret (v6.094) nearZeroVar (freqCut = 85/15, uniqueCut = 50), plus removal of loci with methylation <10% or methylation range <10% across samples

SNP identification from merged BAMs and removal of SNP-overlapping CpGs with BS-Snper (v1.0), parameters --minhetfreq 0.1, --minhomfreq 0.85, --minquali 15, --mincover 10, --maxcover 1000, --minread2 2, --errorate 0.02, --mapvalue 20

Bayesian GLMM age-association screen with rstanarm (v2.26.1) stan_glmer(matrix(c(M,U), ncol=2) ~ Age + (1|Sex)), iter=8000, family=binomial(logit), convergence/effective-size and p<0.05 selection rules — no RNG seed or chain/warmup settings reported, so MCMC output is not bitwise reproducible
Imputation of missing methylation values with the mice R package (v3.16.0) — no method, m, maxit, or seed reported

Epigenetic clock model selection with glmnet (v4.1-8): 70/30 train-test split over 100 bootstrap iterations, 7 iterative lasso rounds retaining the top 75% age-correlated CpGs via cv.glmnet (alpha=0, nfold=10, family='gaussian', type.measure='mae', standardize=false), then a custom function randomly subsetting to n=650 over 500 iterations with alpha=0.02, selecting the lowest-MAE model (111 final loci) — the custom wrapper functions live only in the 404 repository and no RNG seed is reported

Genomic-context annotation of age-associated CpG loci against the haddock genome GFF (reference 85) using GenomicRanges (v1.56.2) and IRanges (v2.38.1), with promoter = 200 bp upstream of gene start and terminator = 200 bp downstream of gene end
Directional (hypo/hyper) methylation classification by per-locus z-score followed by k-means clustering into two clusters in base R (v4.2.0) — no package/function, nstart, or seed reported

Functional/pathway enrichment of CDS sequences from genes with >10 age-associated CpG loci in STRING (v12.0), using Gadus morhua as reference organism, minimum interaction score 0.7 (high confidence), sub-networks via k-means clustering — run through the STRING web service, no script or exported query in prose

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: All 17 computational steps sit at the RI ceiling. Version pinning in this paper is unusually complete for prose (FastQC v0.11.9, MultiQC v1.16, TrimGalore! v0.6.5, Samtools v1.9, Bismark v0.24.2, bedtools v2.29.0, R v4.2.0, caret v6.094, BS-Snper v1.0, rstanarm v2.26.1, mice v3.16.0, glmnet v4.1-8, GenomicRanges v1.56.2, IRanges v2.38.1, STRING v12.0), but no lockfile, container digest, or conda environment is claimed anywhere, so version is capped at 1 (exact pins without environment closure). The stated code repository github.com/emmastrand/Epigenetic_ageing is 404, so code cannot exceed 1 (reconstructable from prose) and the bespoke bootstrap/subsetting model-selection wrapper (C14) is not retrievable at all. Several stochastic steps (C12 MCMC, C13 imputation, C14 bootstrap/subsampling, C16 k-means) report no RNG seed, so exact numerical reproduction of the 111-locus final clock is not attainable from prose even if the environment were rebuilt.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 full-text Methods prose. 4 wet-lab/physical steps (trawl-survey fin-clip and otolith collection; otolith sectioning and annuli age reading; Qiagen DNeasy DNA extraction; Pico Methyl-Seq WGBS library prep and Illumina NovaSeq S4 sequencing) counted in W, out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: Data Availability statement - author analysis code repository
gaps.missing: The paper states 'All data and code used to produce results, and complete analyses are available at https://github.com/emmastrand/Epigenetic_ageing', but that URL returns HTTP 404 and the repository does not appear in the public repository list of GitHub user emmastrand (12 public repos, none named Epigenetic_ageing). No analysis code, no README, and no 'protocols and lab work' folder is retrievable. The companion notebook repo github.com/emmastrand/GMGI_Notebook does resolve (200).
gaps.how_to_close: Make the repository public, or deposit an archived snapshot (Zenodo DOI / Software Heritage identifier) and cite that identifier in the Data Availability statement.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment (HPC shell tools + R stack)
gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image/digest, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock, or module list is claimed. Exact versions are given per tool in prose, but there is no dependency closure for the R 4.2.0 session (Bioconductor release, Stan/rstan toolchain behind rstanarm, compiler) or for the HPC module stack.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container digest covering FastQC/MultiQC/TrimGalore/Samtools/Bismark/bedtools/BS-Snper plus an renv.lock for the R analysis, and state the Bioconductor release used.

gaps.where: Stochastic modelling steps C12 (rstanarm MCMC), C13 (mice imputation), C14 (bootstrap 70/30 split, 500-iteration random n=650 subsetting), C16 (k-means)
gaps.missing: No RNG seeds, chain/warmup counts (C12), imputation method/m/maxit (C13), or k-means nstart (C16) are reported. The final 111-locus clock depends on unpublished random draws, so numeric results are not reproducible even given the same data and versions.
gaps.how_to_close: Report and set explicit seeds (set.seed / stan_glmer(seed=)), report chains/warmup/m/maxit/nstart, and publish the wrapper scripts that perform the bootstrap and subsetting.

gaps.where: Reference genome and annotation used by C4, C15 (and the protein FASTA feeding C17)
gaps.missing: The haddock genome, GFF, and protein FASTA are cited only as bibliographic reference 85; no assembly accession, assembly version, or annotation release is given inline in Methods. By contrast the E. coli spike-in reference is properly pinned (ASM584v2 / GCF_000005845.2).
gaps.how_to_close: State the haddock assembly accession and version plus the annotation release used (e.g. GCA/GCF accession + annotation release date), as done for the E. coli control.

gaps.missing: Trawl-survey fin-clip and otolith collection, otolith sectioning and annuli age reading, Qiagen DNeasy DNA extraction, and Pico Methyl-Seq WGBS library prep + Illumina NovaSeq S4 sequencing are physical sequence- and phenotype-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted. Note that the otolith ages are the response variable of the clock and their provenance is a lab-reading procedure, not a computational artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproducible entry point is the raw WGBS data at NCBI BioProject PRJNA1345711 together with the otolith-age metadata table.
